top_buys.pitch: An oral obesity pill that also treats sleep apnea opens a second large indication ahead of a year-end FDA filing.
top_buys.why: Lilly said Foundayo eased moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea in a late-stage trial and it will file for US approval by year-end. A pill is far cheaper to manufacture and distribute than injections, so each new label expands a market Lilly can actually supply. Health care has also been one of the better sectors over the past week as money rotates out of AI.
top_buys.risks: Obesity-drug competition is fierce and pricing pressure or an FDA delay could cap the upside; Lilly is already a large, well-owned stock so much optimism is priced.
top_buys.watch: Confirmation of the FDA filing before year-end and any detail on pricing for the oral formulation.

top_buys.pitch: A boring, cash-generative defensive that quietly benefits from both cheaper diesel and the rotation away from AI volatility.
top_buys.why: Falling crude lowers diesel costs for a business that runs thousands of trucks, and the inflation relief shows up with a lag in margins. Investors are explicitly looking to diversify away from the volatile AI trade into cheap, capital-returning names. Waste collection revenue is contracted and inflation-linked, so the cost drop drops to the bottom line.
top_buys.risks: Waste stocks move slowly, so the upside is limited, and a renewed oil spike would erase the fuel benefit.
top_buys.watch: Diesel price trends and Q4 guidance commentary on fuel surcharges.

top_buys.pitch: Boeing admitting its production ramp is too slow directly means fewer fuselages ordered from its biggest supplier.
top_buys.why: Boeing is cutting 5% of its commercial airplane workforce because output is rising slower than planned. Spirit's volumes and cash flow are tied almost one-for-one to Boeing's build rates, so a slower ramp pushes out its own recovery. The market focused on Boeing's shares Monday and may be slow to work through the supply chain.
top_buys.risks: Spirit is in the process of being absorbed into Boeing, which cushions downside and makes the stock move on deal news rather than fundamentals.
top_buys.watch: Boeing's monthly delivery figures and any update on 737 production rate targets.

top_buys.pitch: Diversified industrial with aerospace aftermarket and automation exposure that benefits from lower energy input costs.
top_buys.why: Falling crude lowers input and freight costs across industrials, a sector that lagged (-0.2%) last week while the broad market rallied. Honeywell's aerospace aftermarket is tied to flying hours, which are strong heading into the holidays. It is a low-volatility name in a market still digesting AI-bubble fears.
top_buys.risks: Industrial demand could soften if the economy cools, and Boeing production delays touch parts of the aerospace supply chain.
top_buys.watch: US inflation data this week and airline capacity announcements.

top_buys.pitch: Banks rallied as Morgan Stanley's private-markets deal revived the IPO-wealth theme and deal flow stays heavy.
top_buys.why: Monday saw Goldman up 5% as rivals pushed deeper into private-company stock plumbing, and the headline list is full of M&A: JSR, Greenfire, Smartways, RBC's Australian asset manager. Lower oil easing inflation fears supports Fed-cut bets, which historically helps capital-markets activity. Goldman earns fees on both advisory and IPO-adjacent wealth flows.
top_buys.risks: One executive already warned the deal pipeline may be lumpier than it looks, and a market drawdown shuts the IPO window quickly.
top_buys.watch: IPO filings in the coming weeks and this week's inflation print.
